title: Finite coefficients admit prime-field extension trees
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme, $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $F$ a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-constructible-constructible]. Then $F$ has a finite prime-field extension tree in the sense of [def-v2-prime-field-filtration]. No curve or cohomological hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, second proof paragraph; Lemma 03RZ (constructible weak Serre property)

proof.text: The additive order N of 1 in the finite ring is positive and annihilates every module. Integer Chinese remainder idempotents split F into finitely many primary summands. Each summand is a kernel of an endomorphism of F and hence constructible.

For a primary summand killed by r^e, use induction on e. A sheaf killed by r has its canonical prime-field structure on sections and restrictions. Finite locally constant module values on a constructible stratification remain finite locally constant prime-field values, with the same underlying abelian sheaf. This is the prime constructor.

For e>1 take K=F[r] and Q=F/K. The sequence 0->K->F->Q->0 is short exact, K is killed by r, and Q by r^(e-1). Kernel and cokernel constructibility give the constructor hypotheses; apply the base case and induction, then the extension constructor.

Assemble the finitely many primary summands by split short exact sequences. If N=1, F is zero and is a prime factor represented by the zero F_2-sheaf; empty schemes and zero coefficients are included.
